in.rationale: Anil et al. introduce prover-verifier games with one untrusted prover and one trusted verifier on decision problems. Hammond and Adam-Day define a generalised PVG as a messaging game among n_p provers and n_v verifiers on probabilistic decision problems, starting from a common input and ending with a deciding verifier's 0/1 output, so the single-prover, single-verifier game is a special case.

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors introduce Prover-Verifier Games (PVGs), in which a trusted verifier network tries to choose the correct answer to a decision problem and a more powerful but untrusted prover network tries to persuade the verifier of a particular answer regardless of its correctness, so that a reliable justification protocol emerges. They analyse simultaneous and sequential variants, identify a subset that provably has the desired equilibria, and report on two algorithmic tasks that the verifier learns a robust decision rule that still works when it is frozen and the prover's messages are directly optimized to convince it.
title: Prover-Verifier Games: untrusted strong prover, trusted weak verifier, checkable answers
